29th Division left Brittany on 24 September to rejoin First Army and its command post is next listed in the Netherlands on 29 September (rail and motor move of about 800 km).
6th Armored Division moved from Brittany to the Third Army front in Lorraine in mid-September; the Green Book gives the move and the CMH list dates the two command posts.

7th Armored Division, landed at Omaha Beach, was ordered on 13 August to pass through Le Mans to La Ferté-Bernard and on 14 August to attack toward Dreux; the Green Book describes the hurried road march.
Panzer Lehr was ordered up on 7 June for a 90-mile drive from the Chartres area to the Thury-Harcourt assembly areas (documented relocation in C0038).

Pont-l'Abbé here is the hamlet astride Picauville and Étienville (Manche); the stored point is the Étienville commune centroid. The one stored geocoder candidate for the name is Pont-l'Abbé in Finistère, 265 km away, a namesake.

Deliberate conflict group G024: the text of the Lexikon page puts the 716th Static Division in southern France (Thuir) by 10 July 1944 and its own table puts it in Normandy for July; both rows are kept; since 28 October 2026 C0815 is preferred and C0816 alternate (Riviera to the Rhine ch. 4 p. 66 has the division in the IV Luftwaffe Field Corps sector in southern France at the 15 August landing).

The two rows record the places where the German High Command signed the surrender on 7 May (Reims) and on 8 May (Berlin); they are signing places of OKW representatives, not a headquarters move (CMH ch. 19 p. 475).

Deliberate conflict group G028: Wikipedia puts the 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division in Karlsruhe on 3 April 1945, de Lattre (pp. 434-437) puts it at Bruchsal that day and gives Karlsruhe on 4 April to the 9th Colonial Division; both rows are kept, the Bruchsal row is preferred.

The month-level Lexikon row of 15 October 1944 (Saarbrücken, approximate date) and the Ellis row of 14 October (Venlo reserve) cannot both hold on those days; the Lexikon listing is read as the first half of October and both rows are kept at 0.3 (see their Review notes).

12th SS Panzer Division marched overnight 6/7 June 1944 from its station near Évreux (C2060, Annex 1 of FMS B-466, from map, approximate) to the Caen assembly areas, about 110 km (FMS B-466 p. 23; Ellis vol. I pp. 198-206).

First elements of the 198th Division move by motor vehicle and rail from the Burgundian Gate to the LXIV Corps in the Rhine plain, arriving on 27 November (FMS B-263, German p. 27), the day after other battalions fought at Seppois (de Lattre p. 277); the Sélestat point is a representative point at 25 km precision.
